title: R Shiny Apps
text:
These apps run on your machine



Every R package listed here includes a Shiny app. The apps run locally in R — install the package from CRAN and launch from your console. There is no hosted version: the service that previously hosted these apps is no longer under my control, so rather than ship links that fail, each card below gives you the exact command.

title: R Shiny Apps
text:
Regression and modeling




olsrr
Build linear regression models and iterate through specifications quickly. Produces full olsrr model output from the UI.
install.packages("olsrr")
olsrr::ols_launch_app()







blorr
Build, validate and monitor binary logistic regression models with comprehensive output, model fit and validation statistics.
install.packages("blorr")
blorr::blr_launch_app()







xplorerr
One app, seven entry points. Linear and logistic regression, descriptive statistics, inference, RFM analysis, distributions and the visualizer.
install.packages("xplorerr")
xplorerr::app_linear_regression()
Also available: app_descriptive(), app_visualizer(), app_logistic_regression(), app_inference(), app_rfm_analysis(), app_vistributions().

title: R Shiny Apps
text:
Statistics




descriptr
Generate and visualize descriptive statistics for numeric and categorical data. Explore key statistical distributions with interactive plots.
install.packages("descriptr")
descriptr::ds_launch_shiny_app()







inferr
Beginner-friendly hypothesis testing with parametric and non-parametric tests, flexible input options and structured results.
install.packages("inferr")
inferr::ifr_launch_shiny_app()







vistributions
Visualize probability distributions and run statistical quality checks on univariate data.
install.packages("vistributions")
vistributions::vdist_launch_app()

title: R Shiny Apps
text:
Customer analytics




rfm
Customer segmentation using recency, frequency and monetary value analysis. Build customized segments from customer- or transaction-level data.
install.packages("rfm")
rfm::rfm_launch_app()









nse2r has no app



nse2r exported an nse_app() Shiny entry point, but the package was archived on CRAN on 2023-08-07 and is under revival, so it is deliberately excluded from this page rather than shipped with a command that cannot be run. See Packages for its current status.

I build statistical software that holds up outside a tutorial, and I help teams do the same. Author of 11 R packages with 2.8M+ CRAN downloads and 6 open textbooks. Founder of Rsquared Academy, an open-source education platform for data science.
I earned my postgraduate degree from Madras School of Economics (Anna University), Chennai. Most of my work sits at the intersection of R, statistics, economics and finance. Previously I built tooling at Rsquared Computing; I now maintain my own package portfolio independently. Based in Bengaluru, India.

title: Aravind Hebbali
text:
Consulting & Advisory
Model validation and econometric audits. Independent review of specification, identification and inference. You get a written report, not just a fixed script.
Custom package development and architecture. Internal R or Python tooling built to survive handover: documented, tested, and structured so your team can extend it without me.
Team masterclasses. Tidyverse, SQL, command-line tooling. Hands-on sessions built around your own data and problems.
Who this is for: teams shipping quantitative work that other people have to maintain. Who it is not for: one-off analyses, or anyone looking for a pre-packaged answer.

title: R Packages
text:
Archived






nse2r — archived, under revival



nse2r fetched live data from the National Stock Exchange of India. It was archived on CRAN on 2023-08-07 at the maintainer’s request and is currently being revived, so it is no longer installable from CRAN.
Its ~22,000 historical downloads remain part of the totals quoted elsewhere on this site, but that figure is frozen and will not grow. Source and issue tracker: github.com/rsquaredacademy/nse2r.

title: E-Books
text: Six open textbooks, free to read online. Written with blogdown and hosted on Rsquared Academy; each was grown out of posts on my blog and is kept free and ad-free.

title: E-Books
text:
About these books
They began as blog posts, expanded into tutorials on Rsquared Academy, then collected and rewritten into these short books. The writing style is intentionally plain — short chapters, worked examples, and the parts of the documentation people usually skip.
None of them is a substitute for the official R documentation. If you want one resource to start with, Introduction to R is the one.
